rv.q: And that's not all: "Jelly's Last Jam," a show in part about what it means to be African-American, is itself an attempt to remake the Broadway musical in a mythic, African-American image. Wolfe wants nothing less than to do for popular theater what Morton and his peers once did for pop music.
Fortunately, there’s genius in that approach to playing Morton, who never seems to care what we think of him.
Still, you might not be convinced that Morton deserves our absolution—or the credit he repeatedly insists on as “the inventor of Jazz.”
